chose: work in a fresh git worktree of the coherence repo (coherence-conjecture, branch conjecture-record)
over: work in the planetizer worktree the harness actually handed me
because: the brief named repo=coherence and warned a concurrent agent is editing coherence/src, but the cwd I was given was a PLANETIZER worktree — the two disagreed. A worktree off coherence@main honours both halves: right repo, and isolated from coherence-novelty (a03ce10) and from main. Also found the worktree had no node_modules, so the first npm test read as 22 failing files; npm install made it 289 pass / 0 fail.

chose: src/decisions.ts contains a raw 0x00 byte, and the id hash joins its fields on it rather than on a space
because: the Edit tool could not match a literal source line, which is the tell that the bytes are not what they render as
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
a paste/editor artifact that has been silently riding along since the journal landed
deliberate: NUL is the one byte a field cannot contain, so it cannot be forged
discriminatedBy: recompute every stored id in .coherence/decisions/ under both separators and count exact matches

chose: a paste/editor artifact — but one that is now load-bearing, so it stays
because: measured: all 20 non-session entries in this repo's own .coherence/decisions/ reproduce their stored id under join(NUL), 0 of 20 under join(space). The byte is real, committed at HEAD, and load-bearing. Kept it exactly, rewrote it as an explicit \u0000 escape with a named ID_SEP so it stops being invisible, and pinned it with a test.

chose: the shipped agent instruction never mentions the conjecture verb, yet the whole feature depends on agents reaching for it unprompted
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
discriminatedBy: unknown — needs a real fan-out where half the agents get the added instruction line and half do not, counted over conjecture writes per session

chose: no coupling from a resolution to a decide entry — resolution carries --as and --because, and nothing else
over: coherence resolved <id> --into <decision-id>, validated against the journal like retract validates its target
a resolves/resolvedInto field pair on DecisionRecord
because: the arc noticed -> tested -> chose is already CONTENT in --as (which candidate won) and --because (what the test showed); a pointer adds referential integrity to keep in sync and a choreography cost (log the decision, copy its id, then resolve) against a journal whose stated design constraint is that the write must be the cheapest thing in the CLI. It also creates an expectation the arc SHOULD be recorded, which is the incentive-to-be-complete the journal explicitly rejects. What would change my mind: a graph//timeline render where edges do work — today it is text, and the merged timeline is already time-ordered, so the pointer saves a reader one scroll.

chose: candidates live in a new couldBe field, never in over
over: reuse over[] for candidate explanations and avoid touching the record shape
because: over means REJECTED. Candidates are precisely what has NOT been rejected — that is the definition of an open conjecture. Reusing it would have counted every unanswered question in the render's 'N alternative(s) rejected' tally, inverting the one distinction the record exists to make. src/decisions.ts resolve() therefore also keeps conjectures out of standing[] entirely.

chose: the instrument candidate is guaranteed at the WRITE (withInstrumentCandidate in decisions.ts write()), with a deliberately narrow keyword heuristic deciding only the WORDING
over: add it in cli.ts so the library stays neutral
add it at the render so nothing on disk is synthesised
require the author to supply it and warn when they do not
because: at the write it is inside the content hash, so a re-logged conjecture still dedupes to one id, and every path in (CLI, hook, test, future tool) gets it. The heuristic's failure mode is asymmetric ON PURPOSE: a false negative prepends a redundant canonical candidate (noise, recoverable); a false positive would ship a conjecture with no instrument doubt at all (silent, and the exact failure this record exists to prevent). Demonstrated live: 'a paste/editor artifact' did NOT trip the heuristic, so the canonical line was added alongside it.

chose: open conjectures render ABOVE Standing, and --open is a lens that shows nothing else
over: a section at the bottom next to Retracted and Could not
a flag on the existing standing list rather than its own section
because: a standing decision is settled and will still be there tomorrow; an open conjecture DECAYS, because the agent that saw the surprising number is gone and nobody else knows to look. Filed under the settled work it reads as an appendix, which is indistinguishable from never having recorded it. Negative control C4 (emit the section after Standing instead of before) turned 12 assertions red including the explicit ordering pin.

chose: add the conjecture fields to the id hash ONLY when present, and rewrite the invisible NUL separator as an explicit escape
over: widen the hash unconditionally for a uniform formula
leave the raw 0x00 byte alone since it works
because: unconditional widening appends two separators to every plain decision and re-mints every id ever written, orphaning every supersedes pointer in every committed .coherence/decisions/ — silently. Negative control C2 confirmed: 4 assertions red on the literal legacy id d-de1bd779. The escape is behaviour-identical and stops the next reader tidying an invisible byte into a space.

chose: verify that agents actually reach for `coherence conjecture` unprompted
because: it needs a real multi-agent fan-out with the instruction line present vs absent, counted over conjecture writes per session. Everything shipped here is mechanism; whether the verb gets USED is a behavioural question this worktree cannot answer. Logged as the open conjecture d-04198572 with its discriminating test.

chose: the discriminating test is REQUIRED on a conjecture while candidates are optional
over: make both optional so nothing can block a write
make both required, since a conjecture with one candidate is a hunch
because: the asymmetry looks backwards and is not. Candidates are optional because the highest-prior one is supplied by withInstrumentCandidate whether you name it or not, so the field can never be empty. The test is required because without it the entry is a COMPLAINT: a surprising number with no way to settle it is exactly the record that sits in a journal forever being re-noticed. 'unknown — no test comes to mind' is a legal and informative value, so requiring the flag forces the abductive move to completion without ever being able to block a write. If a later pass makes it optional, this is what it is undoing. src/cli.ts, the conjecture branch.

chose: the resolve-target rule and both of its refusal messages live in decisions.ts (resolvableConjecture), not in cli.ts
over: keep the guard inline in the cli.ts resolved branch, next to the other arg checks
spawn dist/cli.js from the test suite to cover it where it sat
because: the requirement was a test for resolving an unknown id, and the guard sat in cli.ts where nothing in test/ can reach it — this suite never spawns the CLI. Moving it makes the rule testable without a process, gives it one write site so a second caller cannot reimplement it differently, and keeps the two DISTINCT refusals together: an id nobody wrote vs an id naming the wrong KIND. Accepting the second would append a resolution no render ever reads — a command that exits 0 and does nothing, which is the defect this harness exists to hunt.
